note:
staging takes 1.4.3. One release is crossed, 1.4.2 to 1.4.3, and nothing is
skipped, so no skipped release carries a landing section anybody has to read.

The releases: class fix, disruption quiet. No core floor moves. Codex stays at
0.147.0 and Claude stays at 2.1.227, the same values 1.4.2 declared.

The box, measured on staging at 19:19Z before this note was written:
claw-members holds one person, that person's persistent core is installed and
reads 2.1.227, which meets the floor. No member reads as below a floor, so this
claw's own classifier will not defer the release to the quiet window.

From this release the wake rail reads the settings file a claw-admin edits. The
file is /etc/commonclaw/bus-nudge.conf, which is where every run has written it,
and the program had been looking at another path, so the rail ran on its shipped
defaults on every claw and a key written into that file changed nothing.

An apply now restarts a running wake unit whose program changed. Before this,
the update replaced the program and left the process running the bytes it
started with, so a wake-rail fix reached the machine and did not reach the
member until somebody restarted the unit or the box was rebooted.
